title: Great Book Chapter 78 — Cosmic Potato / Large-Scale-Structure Morphology Audit
status: book-derived astronomy/cosmology archaeology + quantitative morphology proposal
source: The Great Book Of Potato2.odt, Chapter 78, parsed pages 540-543
historical_thesis: The chapter visually combines Laniakea, Perseus-Pisces and other cosmic-web structures into rounded/oblong 'potato' forms and proposes recurring potato-like morphology across cosmic, biological and quantum scales.
important_recovery: This is a distinct early macro-cosmic shape program, not merely later 11D/Sagittarius-A* material. It should be preserved because it supplies an explicit testable question: are selected cosmic structures quantitatively tuber-like/ellipsoidal, or is the resemblance produced by viewing choice and pattern recognition?

laniakea.book_use: Our home supercluster and one half of an overlapping cosmic-potato picture.
laniakea.modern_status: The 2014 Laniakea definition is a basin-of-attraction construction from peculiar-velocity flows, roughly 160 Mpc across in that analysis. It is not a sharply bounded solid object. Newer Cosmicflows-4 reconstruction gives a slight probabilistic preference for the Laniakea region to be part of a larger Shapley basin of attraction.
laniakea.consequence: The project's shape should be treated as dataset/method/scale dependent, not an immutable cosmic outline.

perseus_pisces.book_claim: Described as a filamentary structure stretching across billions of light-years and visually overlapping Laniakea into an oval/potato.
perseus_pisces.correction: Modern nearby-universe catalogues describe Perseus-Pisces as a prominent filamentary supercluster on scales of tens to over one hundred Mpc depending definition and tracer, not a simple billion-light-year oval. It is normally analyzed as a filamentary/branched complex.
perseus_pisces.consequence: Its natural null model is a filament/network, not an ellipsoid.

overlap_claim.audit: The book's two-overlapping-ovals picture is not a standard astronomical result. Laniakea and Perseus-related attraction/structure can be neighboring or connected in larger flow/network reconstructions, but 'overlapping potato ovals' is a project visualization that must be tested against actual 3D coordinates/fields.

energy_dimensions.book_use: The chapter calls gravitational flow/dark-matter density 'energy dimensions' alongside spatial and temporal dimensions.
energy_dimensions.correction: Density, velocity, gravitational potential and energy are fields/observables on spacetime, not additional dimensions in the geometric sense. Keep coordinate dimension separate from feature dimension.

subatomic_shape.book_use: The chapter suggests particles/fields share spherical or oblong potato-like forms.
subatomic_shape.correction: Elementary particles are not generally little solid spheres/ovals. Spatial probability densities and field configurations can have spherical, axial, nodal or more complicated symmetry depending state, interaction and observable. Visual similarity is not scale invariance.

quantitative_shape_program.data_object: A 3D point cloud, density field rho(x), velocity field v(x), or thresholded excursion set Omega_nu={x:rho(x)>=nu}; choose one before measuring shape.
quantitative_shape_program.center_and_tensor: For weighted points x_i with center x_bar, define a covariance/inertia-like tensor Q=(1/W) sum_i w_i (x_i-x_bar)(x_i-x_bar)^T. Eigenvalues/eigenvectors supply principal axes and orientation.
quantitative_shape_program.axis_ratios: If sqrt(lambda_1)>=sqrt(lambda_2)>=sqrt(lambda_3), define q=b/a=sqrt(lambda_2/lambda_1), s=c/a=sqrt(lambda_3/lambda_1). A tuber-like ellipsoid should occupy a declared region of (q,s), not merely 'look organic'.
quantitative_shape_program.filament_test: Compare ellipsoidal fit against filament/skeleton models. Perseus-Pisces in particular should be expected to score strongly as filamentary under many definitions.
quantitative_shape_program.minkowski_functionals: For a thresholded 3D region, measure volume V, surface area S, integrated mean curvature C and Euler characteristic chi. These distinguish bulk shape, boundary complexity and topology.
quantitative_shape_program.shapefinders: One common convention uses thickness T=3V/S, breadth B=S/C and length L=C/(4 pi), then planarity P=(B-T)/(B+T) and filamentarity F=(L-B)/(L+B). Exact normalization/convention must be stated.
null_models: randomized point cloud preserving radial selection function
cosmological simulation structures selected by the same algorithm
quantitative_shape_program.potato_hypothesis: Define H_Potato before fitting, e.g. compact irregular ellipsoid with bounded axis ratios and nonzero surface roughness but low filamentarity. Compare its out-of-sample fit/information criterion to filament and ellipsoid baselines.
quantitative_shape_program.viewpoint_rule: A 2D projection can make a filament or wall look oval. A cosmic-potato claim must survive 3D reconstruction and reasonable rotations/viewpoints.

cross_scale_rule: Do not claim universal potato morphology merely because rounded shapes occur at multiple scales. A genuine scale-invariant claim would need a common dimensionless statistic or scaling law measured across independently defined systems.
e8_neighbor_correction: Chapter 82 immediately following Chapter 78 calls E8 '248 dimensions'. Existing repository audits correctly repair this: 248 is the dimension of the E8 Lie algebra/adjoint representation, while E8 has rank 8; it is not a claim of 248 ordinary spacetime dimensions.
modern_data_targets: Cosmicflows peculiar-velocity reconstructions for attraction-basin morphology
CLASSIX or comparable cluster catalogues for Perseus-Pisces membership/shape
public galaxy redshift catalogues for 3D point-cloud/skeleton comparison
cosmological simulations for null distributions of shape descriptors
